catalog.name: Soil Moisture
catalog.description: Satellite-derived soil moisture products from multiple NASA missions providing critical information for drought monitoring, agricultural management, and hydrological modeling. These datasets measure volumetric water content in the top few centimeters of soil.

info.name: Attribution
info.content: Data provided by NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS). SMAP mission team at NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory. CYGNSS mission at University of Michigan. GCOM-W1/AMSR2 by JAXA and NASA. Contact: earthdata-support@nasa.gov

info.name: License
info.content: NASA data is generally available for public use. Please check individual dataset licenses and cite appropriately.

info.name: Scientific Applications
info.content: Drought early warning, agricultural water management, flood forecasting, climate model validation, water resource planning, and ecosystem monitoring.

members.name: SMAP Soil Moisture
members.description: Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) mission provides high-quality soil moisture measurements using L-band microwave radiometry with global coverage every 2-3 days.

members.name: SMAP L3 Soil Moisture (9km, Daily)
members.description: Daily global soil moisture from SMAP L-band radiometer at 9km resolution. Measures volumetric water content in top 5cm of soil.

info.name: Background
info.content: SMAP uses L-band (1.4 GHz) microwave radiometry to measure soil moisture in the top 5 cm of soil. L-band microwaves can penetrate through vegetation and clouds, making it ideal for all-weather soil moisture monitoring.

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 9 km spatial resolution, global coverage between 85.044°N and 85.044°S

info.name: Temporal Coverage
info.content: April 2015 to present, with daily global coverage every 2-3 days

info.name: Measurement Units
info.content: Volumetric soil moisture content in cm³/cm³ (or m³/m³)

info.name: Applications
info.content: Drought monitoring, agricultural irrigation scheduling, flood forecasting, numerical weather prediction, climate studies

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA SMAP mission team, NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology

members.name: SMAP L3 Soil Moisture (36km, Daily)
members.description: Daily global soil moisture from SMAP at 36km resolution, providing longer time series and better temporal consistency.

info.name: Background
info.content: The 36km product provides improved temporal consistency and reduced noise compared to higher resolution products, making it ideal for climate and trend analysis.

info.name: Advantages
info.content: Better signal-to-noise ratio, more consistent time series, suitable for large-scale hydrological modeling and climate applications

info.name: Applications
info.content: Climate monitoring, large-scale hydrological modeling, drought trend analysis, water resource assessment

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA SMAP mission team, NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory

members.name: CYGNSS Soil Moisture
members.description: Cyclone Global Navigation Satellite System (CYGNSS) provides soil moisture estimates using GPS reflection signals with high temporal resolution for tropical and subtropical regions.

members.name: CYGNSS Soil Moisture (Daily)
members.description: Daily soil moisture estimates from CYGNSS GPS reflectometry covering latitudes between 38°N and 38°S with high temporal resolution.

info.name: Background
info.content: CYGNSS uses GPS signals reflected off the Earth's surface to measure soil moisture. The technique, called GNSS Reflectometry (GNSS-R), provides complementary measurements to traditional radiometer-based approaches.

info.name: Spatial Coverage
info.content: Tropical and subtropical regions between 38°N and 38°S latitude

info.name: Temporal Resolution
info.content: High temporal resolution with multiple observations per day over the same area

info.name: Mission Duration
info.content: December 2016 to present, 8-satellite constellation

info.name: Unique Advantages
info.content: High temporal sampling, can penetrate dense vegetation, provides measurements in challenging terrain, complementary to other soil moisture missions

info.name: Applications
info.content: Hurricane and storm intensity forecasting, tropical agriculture monitoring, rapid response to soil moisture changes in dynamic weather conditions

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA CYGNSS mission team, University of Michigan, Southwest Research Institute

members.name: AMSR2 Soil Moisture
members.description: Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer 2 (AMSR2) on GCOM-W1 satellite provides long-term soil moisture measurements with day/night observations.

members.name: AMSR2 Surface Soil Moisture C1-band (Day)
members.description: Daytime surface soil moisture from AMSR2 C1-band measurements, providing global coverage with daily temporal resolution.

info.name: Background
info.content: AMSR2 uses multiple microwave frequencies including C-band (6.9 GHz) to measure soil moisture. The C1-band algorithm is optimized for surface soil moisture retrieval in the top few centimeters of soil.

info.name: Observation Time
info.content: Daytime observations (ascending orbit) around 1:30 PM local time

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 25 km spatial resolution with global coverage

info.name: Mission Period
info.content: May 2012 to present, continuing operations

info.name: Applications
info.content: Complement to SMAP for long-term climate studies, numerical weather prediction, agricultural monitoring in regions with different vegetation conditions

info.name: Attribution
info.content: JAXA GCOM-W1/AMSR2 mission, NASA Global Climate and Weather Modeling Program

members.name: AMSR2 Surface Soil Moisture C1-band (Night)
members.description: Nighttime surface soil moisture from AMSR2 C1-band measurements, providing complementary observations to daytime data.

info.name: Background
info.content: Nighttime soil moisture measurements help capture diurnal cycles and provide more stable conditions for soil moisture retrieval, with reduced influence from vegetation water content variations.

info.name: Observation Time
info.content: Nighttime observations (descending orbit) around 1:30 AM local time

info.name: Advantages
info.content: More stable atmospheric conditions, reduced vegetation effects, better representation of soil water content without daytime heating effects

info.name: Applications
info.content: Diurnal soil moisture analysis, improved agricultural monitoring, validation of land surface models, climate studies

info.name: Attribution
info.content: JAXA GCOM-W1/AMSR2 mission, NASA Global Climate and Weather Modeling Program
